name: A Vancouver lot

place_source.title: Wikidata: Vancouver (Q24639), coordinate location and elevation above sea level

blurb: A suburban Vancouver lot on the wet Pacific coast: a lawn and border backed by Douglas-fir, western red cedar and a bigleaf maple, with a feeder that draws chickadees, crows, robins and the resident Anna's hummingbird, and raccoons and grey squirrels after dark.

facts.text: Vancouver has a temperate oceanic climate (Köppen Cfb), bordering on a warm-summer Mediterranean climate (Csb), with dry summers and very wet autumns and winters.

source.title: Wikipedia: Vancouver
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Vancouver", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: Vancouver is named after George Vancouver, who explored the inner harbour of Burrard Inlet in 1792.

source.title: Wikipedia: Vancouver
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Vancouver", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: Stanley Park, at 405 hectares, is Vancouver's largest park and about one-fifth larger than New York City's Central Park.

source.title: Wikipedia: Stanley Park
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Stanley Park", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: Stanley Park holds 200 species of bird and a large raccoon population, and its grey squirrels descend from eight pairs brought from New York's Central Park in 1909.

source.title: Wikipedia: Stanley Park
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Stanley Park", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: Anna's hummingbird, the official city bird of Vancouver, is a year-round resident of the Pacific Northwest and the northernmost year-round hummingbird.

source.title: Wikipedia: Anna's hummingbird
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Anna's hummingbird", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0
